1.explanation:
1. packages/components/.../overflow-menu.config.js defines the CSS tokens and classnames used by the OverflowMenu. It must be extended to include a new “light” modifier class (e.g. `--light`) and its corresponding style tokens (background, text, divider colors) so the CSS bundle can generate the light variant.
2. packages/components/.../overflow-menu.js generates the component’s class names and should be updated to recognize and emit the new `--light` CSS class when configured.
3. packages/react/src/components/OverflowMenu/OverflowMenu.js is the React wrapper that renders the trigger button and floating menu; it needs a new `light` boolean prop, defaultProps and propTypes, and to conditionally apply the `bx--overflow-menu--light` class when `light={true}`.
4. packages/react/src/components/OverflowMenu/OverflowMenu-story.js should be updated to include a story example demonstrating the `light` variant so designers and developers can preview and test the new style.
5. packages/react/src/components/OverflowMenu/OverflowMenu-test.js must include unit tests covering the new `light` prop and verify that the correct className is applied to the DOM output.
1.bug_scenario: The OverflowMenu trigger and dropdown are rendered in the default (dark‐themed) style: the three-dot icon, menu background, text, and dividers all use gray tones. When placed on a light gray page background (e.g. #f4f4f4), the default gray menu fades into the page and lacks sufficient contrast. The user wants a “light” modifier on <OverflowMenu> (similar to the TextInput “--light” variant) so that the button and menu invert to darker elements on a white/light background and are clearly visible.

2.explanation:
All of these files are involved in defining, styling, rendering, and testing the OverflowMenu component in both the core (web components) library and the React wrapper. 

 1. overflow-menu.config.js — this config drives the CSS class modifiers and scss generation; a new `--light` modifier needs to be declared here.  
 2. overflow-menu.js (core) — the web component implementation must accept a new `light` attribute or `light` property and toggle the `bx--overflow-menu--light` class on the root element.  
 3. OverflowMenu.js (React) — the React wrapper must accept a `light` prop (or similar), pass it through to the underlying markup, and apply the correct `bx--overflow-menu--light` class.  
 4. OverflowMenu-story.js — the Storybook example needs to include a story demonstrating the new light variant.  
 5. OverflowMenu-test.js — tests (and snapshots) must be updated to verify that when the `light` prop is passed, the correct modifier class appears and the styling matches the design intent.
2.bug_scenario: In the live example the OverflowMenu trigger (three‐dot icon) and its dropdown sit on a light‐grey background (#f4f4f4), but the menu itself uses the default grey styling — so the trigger icon and menu blend into the page. We need to add a “light” variant (e.g. `--light` modifier or `light` prop) so that on light backgrounds the icon is darker and the menu background and borders invert appropriately.
